p: Here's the clever bit about Black Park: it puts you within easy reach of some of the best-known days out in the south. Windsor is just down the road, so you could spend the morning up in the pines and the afternoon gazing up at Windsor Castle, or wandering over the bridge into Eton. Families with younger kids often plan a weekend around Legoland Windsor, and a treetop session makes a cracking contrast for the older ones.

Closer still, Langley Park sits right next door, another Buckinghamshire country park known for its gardens and rhododendrons in late spring. Burnham Beeches, with its ancient pollarded trees, is a short drive away and feels properly wild for somewhere so close to the M4.

On the day itself, give yourselves time. Parking at a popular country park on a sunny Saturday can take a while, and you don't want to arrive flustered for a timed briefing. Once you're on the course, the whole thing usually takes a couple of hours, more if the group likes to stop and cheer each other across every bridge.

Bring water, a snack for afterwards and a bag to keep in the car for muddy kit. Long sleeves help on the scramble nets, and a pair of light gloves can save your palms on the ropes. Most of all, bring a sense of humour, because the first wobbly crossing humbles everybody.
